header.title: Pyramid Texts II: Teti: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Pyramid Texts
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:pyramid-texts:teti:translit, from the UD Egyptian-PC treebank of the Pyramid Texts (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.357.590c.2: Line 1: ꞽ:b(ꞽ)ꜣ is uncertain. Line 2: the second clause is literally 'he has not said: he protects you'. Line 5: ś:ḫt is usually 'trap, snare'; ꞽtn taken as a demonstrative.
notes.1.1a: ꜣḫ.t wr.t, Nut's epithet, may also be rendered 'great radiant one'.
notes.355.574b-c: Line 1: mꜥḥꜣ is obscure, perhaps a part of the body parallel to 'arm'. Line 5: ꞽwn(.w) is obscure and 'bound' is a guess; ś:ḥm may mean 'drive back' or 'crush'.
notes.386.679d: Snake spells. Line 1: pꜣs is uncertain. Line 2: č̣śr ṭp ('clear' or 'sacred of head') and nꜣw.(w)t (the snake's lair or a plant) are obscure. Line 3: ḥm-pśč̣.t could also be 'servant of the Ennead'. Line 4: čn(ꞽ) read as 'where?'; šnč taken as the acacia, though that word is normally šnč̣.t. Line 5: śꞽn(.w) uncertain. Line 6: ꞽp(w).t(ꞽ) 'messenger' or 'commission'; sense obscure. ḫr Wr ḫr ḥm-psḏt may also be two parallel clauses: 'The Great One falls; the servant of the Ennead falls.'
notes.364.618a: Line 5: Henu is the sacred bark of Sokar. Line 8 plays on ꜣḫ.tꞽ 'you are an akh' and ꜣḫ.t 'horizon'.
notes.272.392d: Line 1 is obscure: tḫtḫ means 'disordered, tangled', perhaps the dishevelled hair of mourning, but the construction is uncertain. Line 5: mwmw is obscure.
notes.364.614a: Andjeti, the god of Busiris; the name plays on ś:ꜥnḫ 'make live'.

nodes.text: Words to be spoken by Nut, the great effective one: My son, my eldest, is Teti, who opened my womb.
He is not [one for whom] the heads of the gods are dishevelled(?).
It is Teti who judges his case with Him-whose-name-is-hidden, on this day of slaughtering the eldest.
It is Teti who eats their magic,
it is Teti who swallows their *akh*s [spirit-powers].
Whoever he finds on his way, he eats for himself piecemeal(?).
Place your arm on the earth, your *mꜥḥꜣ* in the Great Mound; move about in it among the *akh*s [transfigured spirits].
Stand, raise yourself, like Osiris!
O Osiris Teti, Horus has come to seek you;
he has had Thoth snare for you the followers of Seth,
he has brought them to you bound(?); he has cowed(?) the heart of Seth.
Geb has brought you your two sisters to your side, this Isis and Nephthys.
None of them can get away(?) from him.
Horus has protected you; he did not [merely] say he would protect you.
Horus has taken his Eye from Seth
and has given it to you,
this sweet Eye of his. Catch it for yourself, claim it for yourself.
Words to be spoken: Horus has cried out because of his Eye; Seth has cried out because of his testicles.
Horus has made you live in this your name of Andjeti.
O Osiris Teti, lift up your heart toward him; may your heart be great, may your mouth be open.
O Osiris Teti, you are a powerful god; there is no god like you.
Horus has given you his children, that they may lift you up;
he has given you all the gods, that they may follow you and that you may have power over them.
Horus has raised you up in his name of Henu;
he lifts you up in your name of Sokar.
You live, you move about every day;
you are an *akh* [transfigured spirit] in your name of Horizon, from which Ra comes forth.
Your mother Nut has borne you; Geb has wiped your mouth for you.
Your sister Isis comes to you, rejoicing [for] [love] of you.
Sharp Horus has come forth from you as Horus who is in Sothis.
Horus fell because of his Eye; Seth was stricken(?) because of his testicles.
Clear of head(?), you who are in the *nꜣw.t*: fall down, slither away!
Words to be spoken: The Great One falls before the Majesty of the Ennead.
Words to be spoken: Where is Horus who came forth from the acacia(?)?
Look at Teti! Teti is Horus who came forth from the acacia(?), in haste(?);
no messenger was given to him(?).
